key_insight: QC-DFET embeds surface-reaction active spaces into compact qubit Hamiltonians, enabling correlated quantum simulation of catalytic interfaces while retaining metallic-environment effects.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical path toward predictive, high-accuracy energetics for heterogeneous catalysis and reaction-barrier screening on quantum hardware.
method: Reaction-consistent active-space selection preserves orbital continuity along reaction coordinates.
Quantum-selected configuration interaction uses measurements from the Zuchongzhi superconducting processor to recover static correlation.
Strongly contracted perturbation theory adds dynamic correlation within the embedded framework.
evidence_signal: Validated on Cu(111) through H2 dissociation/desorption, CO adsorption, and formate hydrogenation benchmarks, including active spaces up to 28 qubits and agreement with experimentally constrained barriers and adsorption preferences.
watch_item: The approach still depends on careful active-space construction, embedding accuracy, and hardware measurement quality, which may limit robustness as systems scale.
paper_title: Embedded quantum computing for many-body surface reaction
